da.p: 'da'-letter; the 26th consonant among 41 syllables; the 18th letter among 33 consonants;  3rd letter which has to rely on a vowel, of dental group among five groups of different pronunciation groups. It has four types of 'da'. These are: (1) the pronunciation 'd' which can be changed from another letter(changing 'da'=Ādesa=kāriya.); (2) The insertion 'd'(Āgama 'd'.). (3) Dropping 'd' (Lopa-'da'); (4) Suffix 'd', which has to add after the root (Suffix 'da'); See-Dhamma 38, dhamma,ṭṭha,2, 102-3, Nītisutta 97. See-Original. Ti, pi. 10. 1-2.

dā.p: This is the syllable that should be recited in combination with the consonant and vowel. It has three kinds: (1) element, (2) substance, and (3) region.
